models/ols_linear_regression/index.html.step1_title: Residual Sum of Squares (RSS) Loss Formulation
models/ols_linear_regression/index.html.step1_desc: Ordinary Least Squares minimizes the variance of the residuals under the Gauss-Markov assumptions, penalizing squared Euclidean distance between ground truth $y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and linear hypothesis $\hat{y} = X\beta$.
models/ols_linear_regression/index.html.step2_title: Analytical Normal Equation via Gradient Zeroing
models/ols_linear_regression/index.html.step2_formula: $$\nabla_\beta \mathcal{L}_{\text{OLS}}(\beta) = -\frac{1}{n} X^T (y - X\beta) = 0 \implies X^T X \beta = X^T y \implies \hat{\beta} = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T y$$
models/ols_linear_regression/index.html.step2_desc: Because the loss surface is strictly convex when $X$ has full column rank, setting the first-order partial derivative to zero directly yields the unique global minimum without requiring iterative optimization.

models/ridge_regression/index.html.step1_desc: Ridge regression injects an $L_2$ shrinkage penalty weighted by hyperparameter $\lambda \ge 0$. This shrinks non-significant coefficients toward zero, combating multicollinearity and bounding variance.
models/ridge_regression/index.html.step2_formula: $$\nabla_\beta \mathcal{L}_{\text{Ridge}} = -\frac{1}{n}X^T(y - X\beta) + \lambda \beta = 0 \implies \hat{\beta}_{\text{Ridge}} = (X^T X + n\lambda I)^{-1} X^T y$$
models/ridge_regression/index.html.step2_desc: Adding $\lambda I$ to the Gram matrix $X^T X$ ensures the matrix is strictly diagonally dominant and invertible (positive definite), eliminating singularity even when features are perfectly collinear or $p > n$.

models/lasso_regression/index.html.step1_desc: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (Lasso) replaces the smooth $L_2$ penalty with non-smooth $L_1$ norm. The diamond-shaped constraint boundary forces unimportant feature weights exactly to zero, performing intrinsic feature selection.
models/lasso_regression/index.html.step2_desc: Because $|\beta_j|$ is non-differentiable at zero, closed-form matrix inversion is impossible. Lasso is solved iteratively via coordinate descent using the soft-thresholding operator $\mathcal{S}$.

models/elastic_net/index.html.step1_title: Convex Combination of L1 and L2 Penalties
models/elastic_net/index.html.step1_desc: Elastic Net unifies Lasso and Ridge through mixing parameter $\alpha \in [0, 1]$. It preserves Lasso's sparse feature selection while retaining Ridge's grouping effect for clusters of correlated variables.
models/elastic_net/index.html.step2_desc: In each univariate coordinate descent step, the $L_2$ term stabilizes the denominator against collinearity while the $L_1$ soft-thresholding in the numerator enforces sparsity.

models/polynomial_regression/index.html.step1_formula: $$\phi(x) = [1, x_1, x_2, x_1^2, x_1 x_2, x_2^2, \dots, x_p^d]^T, \quad \hat{y} = \phi(x)^T \beta$$
models/polynomial_regression/index.html.step1_desc: Projects original feature vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^p$ into a high-dimensional polynomial feature space $\mathcal{H}$ of degree $d$, allowing linear models to fit complex non-linear curves.
models/polynomial_regression/index.html.step2_title: Expanded Normal Equations in Feature Space
models/polynomial_regression/index.html.step2_desc: Fitting proceeds via ordinary or Ridge linear algebra over design matrix $\Phi$. Higher polynomial degrees $d$ rapidly increase feature correlation, necessitating regularized inversion.

models/robust_regression/index.html.step1_desc: Huber loss blends the efficiency of squared loss for small residuals $|r| \le \delta$ with the outlier resistance of absolute loss for extreme errors $|r| > \delta$.
models/robust_regression/index.html.step2_desc: Weights $w_i$ dynamically downscale leverage points with large residuals, iteratively solving weighted normal equations until convergence.

models/support_vector_regression/index.h.step1_formula: $$\min_{w, b, \xi, \xi^*} \frac{1}{2} \|w\|_2^2 + C \sum_{i=1}^n (\xi_i + \xi_i^*), \quad \text{s.t. } \begin{cases} y_i - w^T \phi(x_i) - b \le \epsilon + \xi_i \\ w^T \phi(x_i) + b - y_i \le \epsilon + \xi_i^* \\ \xi_i, \xi_i^* \ge 0 \end{cases}$$
models/support_vector_regression/index.h.step1_desc: SVR constructs an $\epsilon$-insensitive tube around the regression curve; residuals within distance $\epsilon$ carry zero penalty, ignoring minor noise.
models/support_vector_regression/index.h.step2_desc: Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions ensure only points outside the $\epsilon$-tube become support vectors with non-zero Lagrange multipliers $(\alpha_i - \alpha_i^*)$.

models/knn_regressor/index.html.step1_formula: $$\mathcal{N}_k(x) = \left\{ x_{(1)}, x_{(2)}, \dots, x_{(k)} \right\}, \quad d(x, x_i) = \|x - x_i\|_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^p (x_j - x_{ij})^2}$$
models/knn_regressor/index.html.step1_desc: Identifies the $k$ closest training points in metric space according to Euclidean or Minkowski distance. Proper feature scaling is essential to prevent scale distortion.
models/knn_regressor/index.html.step2_desc: Predicts the target via a weighted average of neighbor labels, smoothly decaying neighbor influence inversely proportional to geometric distance.

models/decision_tree_regressor/index.htm.step1_title: Sum of Squared Errors (SSE) Partitioning Objective
models/decision_tree_regressor/index.htm.step1_desc: Recursively partitions the feature space into axis-aligned hyper-rectangles by picking the feature $j$ and split threshold $s$ that minimizes variance.
models/decision_tree_regressor/index.htm.step2_desc: The tree greedily chooses split $(j^*, s^*) = \arg\max \Delta \text{Var}$, computing node predictions as the local empirical mean $\hat{c}_m = \frac{1}{|D_m|} \sum_{i \in D_m} y_i$.

models/random_forest_regressor/index.htm.step1_desc: Generates $B$ de-correlated regression trees trained on independent bootstrap replicas of the dataset, randomly sampling $m \le p$ candidate split features at each node.
models/random_forest_regressor/index.htm.step2_desc: Random feature subsampling lowers pairwise tree correlation $\rho$. As the ensemble size $B \to \infty$, the second variance term vanishes, drastically reducing total error without increasing bias.

models/gradient_boosting_regressor/index.step1_desc: Builds an additive model in a greedy stage-wise fashion, adding a new shallow tree at each step scaled by learning rate $\eta \in (0, 1]$ to correct existing residuals.
models/gradient_boosting_regressor/index.step2_title: Negative Gradient Pseudo-Residuals & Terminal Node Update
models/gradient_boosting_regressor/index.step2_desc: Rather than fitting labels $y$ directly, tree $m$ fits steepest-descent direction pseudo-residuals $r_{im}$, enabling arbitrary differentiable loss functions (MSE, MAE, Huber).

models/xgboost_regressor/index.html.step1_title: Second-Order Taylor Expansion of the Objective
models/xgboost_regressor/index.html.step1_formula: $$\tilde{\mathcal{L}}^{(t)} \approx \sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_i f_t(x_i) + \frac{1}{2} h_i f_t^2(x_i) \right] + \gamma T + \frac{\lambda}{2} \sum_{j=1}^T w_j^2, \quad g_i = \partial_{\hat{y}} \mathcal{L}, \; h_i = \partial_{\hat{y}}^2 \mathcal{L}$$
models/xgboost_regressor/index.html.step1_desc: XGBoost approximates the loss function using a 2nd-order Taylor expansion, incorporating both 1st-order gradients $g_i$ and 2nd-order Hessians $h_i$ alongside complexity penalty $\gamma T + \frac{\lambda}{2}\|w\|^2$.
models/xgboost_regressor/index.html.step2_title: Optimal Leaf Weights & Split Gain Criterion
models/xgboost_regressor/index.html.step2_formula: $$w_j^* = -\frac{\sum_{i \in I_j} g_i}{\sum_{i \in I_j} h_i + \lambda}, \quad \text{Gain} = \frac{1}{2} \left[ \frac{G_L^2}{H_L + \lambda} + \frac{G_R^2}{H_R + \lambda} - \frac{(G_L + G_R)^2}{H_L + H_R + \lambda} \right] - \gamma$$
models/xgboost_regressor/index.html.step2_desc: Setting the derivative with respect to leaf weight $w_j$ to zero analytically yields optimal leaf scores $w_j^*$ and the exact gain used to evaluate split points.

models/lightgbm_regressor/index.html.step1_formula: $$x_{ij} \mapsto b \in \{0, 1, \dots, 255\}, \quad \mathcal{H}[b] = \left( \sum_{i: x_{ij} \in b} g_i, \, \sum_{i: x_{ij} \in b} h_i \right)$$
models/lightgbm_regressor/index.html.step1_desc: LightGBM discretizes continuous features into discrete 8-bit bins (histograms), slashing memory consumption and replacing $O(n)$ continuous split searches with $O(\text{bins})$ bin aggregations.
models/lightgbm_regressor/index.html.step2_desc: Rather than growing trees level-by-level, LightGBM splits the single leaf with highest loss reduction, achieving lower loss with fewer splits under max-depth constraints.

models/catboost_regressor/index.html.step1_title: Ordered Target Encoding to Prevent Target Leakage
models/catboost_regressor/index.html.step1_formula: $$\hat{x}_k^i = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} [x_{\sigma_j, k} = x_{\sigma_i, k}] y_{\sigma_j} + a \cdot P}{\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} [x_{\sigma_j, k} = x_{\sigma_i, k}] + a}, \quad P = \text{prior target mean}$$
models/catboost_regressor/index.html.step1_desc: CatBoost encodes high-cardinality categorical variables using random permutations $\sigma$. Each example's target encoding relies only on instances appearing prior to it in the permutation, eliminating target leakage.
models/catboost_regressor/index.html.step2_desc: Oblivious trees apply the same split feature and threshold across all nodes at depth $d$. This balanced structure allows vector execution on CPU/GPU and naturally acts as strong regularization.

models/bayesian_linear_regression/index..step1_formula: $$p(w) = \mathcal{N}(0, \alpha^{-1} I), \quad p(y \mid X, w, \beta) = \mathcal{N}(y \mid Xw, \beta^{-1} I)$$
models/bayesian_linear_regression/index..step1_desc: Places an isotropic Gaussian prior over weight vector $w$ with precision $\alpha$. Targets $y$ follow a Gaussian likelihood conditioned on $Xw$ with noise precision $\beta$.
models/bayesian_linear_regression/index..step2_formula: $$p(w \mid X, y) = \mathcal{N}(\mu_N, \Sigma_N), \quad \Sigma_N = (\alpha I + \beta X^T X)^{-1}, \quad \mu_N = \beta \Sigma_N X^T y$$
models/bayesian_linear_regression/index..step2_desc: By Bayesian conjugacy, the posterior distribution is also Gaussian. For query point $x_*$, the predictive variance $\sigma_*^2 = \frac{1}{\beta} + x_*^T \Sigma_N x_*$ provides exact epistemic uncertainty quantification.

models/gaussian_process_regressor/index..step1_desc: A Gaussian Process defines a distribution over continuous functions such that any finite collection of points has a joint multivariate Gaussian distribution defined by kernel covariance $K$.
models/gaussian_process_regressor/index..step2_title: Joint Conditioning for Exact Closed-Form Inference
models/gaussian_process_regressor/index..step2_formula: $$\bar{f}_* = K_*^T (K + \sigma_n^2 I)^{-1} y, \quad \text{Var}(f_*) = K(x_*, x_*) - K_*^T (K + \sigma_n^2 I)^{-1} K_*$$
models/gaussian_process_regressor/index..step2_desc: Query predictions $\bar{f}_*$ and their posterior variances are obtained directly via Schur complement matrix conditioning, delivering calibrated confidence intervals for Bayesian optimization.

models/mlp_regressor/index.html.step1_desc: Passes input vectors through sequential hidden layers composed of affine weight projections followed by element-wise non-linear activations (ReLU, GELU).
models/mlp_regressor/index.html.step2_desc: Applies the chain rule from output loss backward through network layers to compute exact parameter gradients for optimizer updates (Adam, SGD with momentum).

models/logistic_regression/index.html.step1_formula: $$p(y=1 \mid x) = \sigma(w^T x + b) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(w^T x + b)}}, \quad \mathcal{L}_{\text{BCE}}(w) = -\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \left[ y_i \ln p_i + (1 - y_i) \ln(1 - p_i) \right]$$
models/logistic_regression/index.html.step1_desc: Maps real-valued linear logits to calibrated probabilities $[0, 1]$ via the logistic sigmoid function, minimizing the negative log-likelihood of Bernoulli observations.
models/logistic_regression/index.html.step2_formula: $$\nabla_w \mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{n} X^T (p - y) \implies w^{(t+1)} = w^{(t)} - \eta \cdot \frac{1}{n} X^T (p - y)$$
models/logistic_regression/index.html.step2_desc: The gradient exhibits a clean error-residual form $(p_i - y_i) x_i$. Because log-loss is strictly convex, gradient descent or L-BFGS is guaranteed to reach the global minimum.

models/linear_discriminant_analysis/inde.step1_formula: $$J(w) = \frac{w^T S_B w}{w^T S_W w}, \quad S_B = (\mu_1 - \mu_0)(\mu_1 - \mu_0)^T, \quad S_W = \Sigma_0 + \Sigma_1$$
models/linear_discriminant_analysis/inde.step1_desc: LDA seeks a linear projection vector $w$ that simultaneously maximizes between-class variance $S_B$ while minimizing within-class variance $S_W$.
models/linear_discriminant_analysis/inde.step2_formula: $$S_W^{-1} S_B w = \lambda w \implies w^* \propto S_W^{-1} (\mu_1 - \mu_0), \quad \delta_k(x) = x^T \Sigma^{-1} \mu_k - \frac{1}{2} \mu_k^T \Sigma^{-1} \mu_k + \ln P(Y=k)$$
models/linear_discriminant_analysis/inde.step2_desc: Under the assumption of equal class covariance $\Sigma_0 = \Sigma_1 = \Sigma$, the decision boundary is an exact linear hyperplane separating classes in projected space.

models/quadratic_discriminant_analysis/i.step1_desc: Unlike LDA, QDA drops the assumption of shared covariance, allowing each class $k$ to have its own unique covariance matrix $\Sigma_k$.
models/quadratic_discriminant_analysis/i.step2_desc: The quadratic term $x^T \Sigma_k^{-1} x$ does not cancel out across classes, naturally producing quadratic (parabolic, elliptical, hyperbolic) decision boundaries.

models/perceptron/index.html.step1_desc: Penalizes only misclassified samples $\mathcal{M} = \{i \mid y_i (w^T x_i + b) \le 0\}$ with a penalty proportional to how far they violate the decision hyperplane.
models/perceptron/index.html.step2_formula: $$w^{(t+1)} = w^{(t)} + \eta \cdot y_i x_i, \quad b^{(t+1)} = b^{(t)} + \eta \cdot y_i \quad (\text{for } y_i(w^T x_i + b) \le 0)$$
models/perceptron/index.html.step2_desc: According to the Novikoff Perceptron Convergence Theorem, if the dataset is linearly separable with margin $\gamma$, the algorithm converges in at most $(R/\gamma)^2$ mistake steps.

models/gaussian_naive_bayes/index.html.step1_formula: $$P(Y=k \mid X) = \frac{P(Y=k) \prod_{j=1}^p P(X_j \mid Y=k)}{P(X)}, \quad P(X_j \mid Y=k) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi \sigma_{kj}^2}} e^{-\frac{(x_j - \mu_{kj})^2}{2\sigma_{kj}^2}}$$
models/gaussian_naive_bayes/index.html.step1_desc: Assumes that all features $X_j$ are conditionally independent given class label $Y=k$, drastically simplifying parameter estimation from joint distributions to 1D Gaussians.
models/gaussian_naive_bayes/index.html.step2_desc: Computing log-probabilities avoids numerical underflow from small probability products. Parameters $\mu_{kj}, \sigma_{kj}^2$ are estimated in closed form in a single data pass.

models/multinomial_bernoulli_nb/index.ht.step1_formula: $$P(X \mid Y=k) = \prod_{j=1}^p \theta_{kj}^{x_j} (1 - \theta_{kj})^{1 - x_j} \quad (\text{Bernoulli}), \quad P(X \mid Y=k) = \frac{(\sum x_j)!}{\prod x_j!} \prod_{j=1}^p \theta_{kj}^{x_j} \quad (\text{Multinomial})$$
models/multinomial_bernoulli_nb/index.ht.step1_desc: Tailored for count data and discrete token features (such as NLP Bag-of-Words and spam classification), modeling word occurrences or binary word indicators.
models/multinomial_bernoulli_nb/index.ht.step2_desc: Adding smoothing constant $\alpha$ prevents the zero-frequency problem where an unseen word in test data would otherwise zero out the entire posterior probability.

models/support_vector_classifier/index.h.step1_desc: Finds the separating hyperplane that maximizes the geometric margin $2/\|w\|$ while allowing slack $\xi_i$ for non-separable points, controlled by regularization budget $C$.
models/support_vector_classifier/index.h.step2_formula: $$\max_\alpha \sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i,j} \alpha_i \alpha_j y_i y_j K(x_i, x_j) \quad \text{s.t. } 0 \le \alpha_i \le C, \; \sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i y_i = 0$$
models/support_vector_classifier/index.h.step2_desc: Replacing inner products $\langle \phi(x_i), \phi(x_j) \rangle$ with Mercer kernel function $K(x_i, x_j)$ projects features into infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with zero computational overhead.

models/knn_classifier/index.html.step1_formula: $$\mathcal{N}_k(x) = \left\{ x_{(1)}, x_{(2)}, \dots, x_{(k)} \right\}, \quad d_M(x, x') = \sqrt{(x - x')^T \Sigma^{-1} (x - x')}$$
models/knn_classifier/index.html.step1_desc: Constructs a local neighborhood around query point $x$ using Euclidean, Manhattan, or Mahalanobis metric distances, sensitive to feature scaling.
models/knn_classifier/index.html.step2_desc: Classifies the query point via maximum majority vote across the $k$ nearest neighbors. Breakpoints are resolved via distance weighting $w_i = 1/d_i$.

models/decision_tree_classifier/index.ht.step1_title: Node Impurity Criteria: Gini Index & Shannon Entropy
models/decision_tree_classifier/index.ht.step1_formula: $$I_G(t) = 1 - \sum_{k=1}^K p_{tk}^2, \quad H(t) = -\sum_{k=1}^K p_{tk} \log_2(p_{tk}), \quad p_{tk} = \frac{1}{|D_t|} \sum_{i \in D_t} \mathbb{I}(y_i = k)$$
models/decision_tree_classifier/index.ht.step1_desc: Measures the heterogeneity of class distributions within node $t$. Pure nodes have impurity $0$, while evenly distributed classes maximize impurity.
models/decision_tree_classifier/index.ht.step2_formula: $$\Delta I(t, s) = I(D_t) - \frac{|D_L|}{|D_t|} I(D_L) - \frac{|D_R|}{|D_t|} I(D_R) \implies s^* = \arg\max_s \Delta I(t, s)$$
models/decision_tree_classifier/index.ht.step2_desc: The tree greedily evaluates all candidate splits across all features, selecting the split $(j^*, s^*)$ yielding maximum reduction in node impurity.

models/random_forest_classifier/index.ht.step1_formula: $$\hat{C}_b(x) = T_b(x; \Theta_b), \quad m = \lfloor\sqrt{p}\rfloor \text{ candidate features evaluated per split}$$
models/random_forest_classifier/index.ht.step1_desc: Draws $B$ bootstrap samples from training data. At every node, a random subset of $m = \sqrt{p}$ features is evaluated, intentionally de-correlating individual trees.
models/random_forest_classifier/index.ht.step2_desc: Aggregates predictions via plurality vote. The $\approx 36.8\%$ unselected samples in each bootstrap draw provide internal cross-validation without separate holdout sets.

models/adaboost_classifier/index.html.step1_desc: AdaBoost sequentially trains base decision stumps $h_m$ that minimize the exponential loss, putting greater weight on examples misclassified by prior estimators.
models/adaboost_classifier/index.html.step2_formula: $$\epsilon_m = \sum_{i: y_i \ne h_m(x_i)} w_i^{(m)}, \quad \alpha_m = \frac{1}{2} \ln\left( \frac{1 - \epsilon_m}{\epsilon_m} \right), \quad w_i^{(m+1)} = \frac{w_i^{(m)} \exp(-\alpha_m y_i h_m(x_i))}{Z_m}$$
models/adaboost_classifier/index.html.step2_desc: Base classifiers with lower weighted error $\epsilon_m$ receive higher voting weight $\alpha_m$. Correctly predicted samples are downweighted by $\exp(-\alpha_m)$.

models/gradient_boosted_classifiers/inde.step1_formula: $$p_k(x) = \frac{e^{F_k(x)}}{\sum_{j=1}^K e^{F_j(x)}}, \quad \mathcal{L} = -\sum_{k=1}^K y_k \ln p_k(x), \quad g_{ik} = p_k(x_i) - y_{ik}$$
models/gradient_boosted_classifiers/inde.step1_desc: Gradient boosted classification models probability outputs via softmax logit transforms, computing exact negative gradient residuals $g_{ik} = p_{ik} - y_{ik}$.
models/gradient_boosted_classifiers/inde.step2_title: Stage-Wise Tree Fitting to Gradient Residuals
models/gradient_boosted_classifiers/inde.step2_formula: $$F_{km}(x) = F_{k, m-1}(x) + \eta \sum_{j=1}^J \gamma_{jkm} \mathbb{I}(x \in R_{jkm}), \quad \gamma_{jkm} = \frac{\sum_{x_i \in R_j} (y_{ik} - p_{ik})}{\sum_{x_i \in R_j} p_{ik}(1 - p_{ik})}$$
models/gradient_boosted_classifiers/inde.step2_desc: Each stage fits $K$ parallel regression trees to the probability residuals. Terminal node values $\gamma_{jkm}$ are solved using a Newton-Raphson 2nd-order step.

models/stacking_voting_classifiers/index.step1_formula: $$Z = \begin{bmatrix} f_1(x_1) & f_2(x_1) & \dots & f_M(x_1) \\ f_1(x_2) & f_2(x_2) & \dots & f_M(x_2) \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ f_1(x_n) & f_2(x_n) & \dots & f_M(x_n) \end{bmatrix}, \quad f_m \in \{\text{SVC}, \text{RF}, \text{GBDT}, \text{LR}\}$$
models/stacking_voting_classifiers/index.step1_desc: Stacking trains diverse base models across different model families, compiling their out-of-fold probability predictions into a meta-feature matrix $Z$.
models/stacking_voting_classifiers/index.step2_desc: A final meta-classifier (typically regularized Logistic Regression) learns optimal blending weights for the base estimators, preventing overfitting via $K$-fold cross-validation.

models/mlp_classifier/index.html.step1_desc: The final layer applies softmax normalization to convert output activations into mutually exclusive probability distributions over $K$ classes.
models/mlp_classifier/index.html.step2_desc: The combination of Softmax and Cross-Entropy yields the clean difference $(\hat{p} - y)$, flowing backward through hidden layers via the chain rule.

models/convolutional_neural_networks/ind.step1_formula: $$S(i, j) = (I * K)(i, j) = \sum_{m=-M}^M \sum_{n=-N}^N I(i - m, j - n) K(m, n) + b$$
models/convolutional_neural_networks/ind.step1_desc: Slides learnable spatial kernels $K$ across input channels to extract translation-equivariant features (edges, textures, motifs) while sharing parameters across pixel coordinates.
models/convolutional_neural_networks/ind.step2_formula: $$\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial K(m, n)} = \sum_{i, j} \delta(i, j) I(i - m, j - n), \quad P(i, j) = \max_{u, v \in \Omega} S(i+u, j+v)$$
models/convolutional_neural_networks/ind.step2_desc: Max-pooling reduces spatial resolution and grants local translation invariance. Gradients flow back during backpropagation exclusively through the winning max unit.

models/transformers_rnn_classifier/index.step1_formula: $$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) V, \quad Q = X W_Q, \; K = X W_K, \; V = X W_V$$
models/transformers_rnn_classifier/index.step1_desc: Computes pairwise affinity scores between all tokens in a sequence simultaneously. The scaling factor $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ prevents dot products from growing excessively large, avoiding vanishing gradients.
models/transformers_rnn_classifier/index.step2_desc: Multiple attention heads allow the network to simultaneously attend to information from different representation subspaces. Sequence-level decisions are pooled from the [CLS] embedding.

models/kmeans_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Partitions $n$ observations into $K$ disjoint clusters such that the sum of squared Euclidean distances from each data point to its assigned centroid $\mu_k$ is minimized.
models/kmeans_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: Alternates between: (1) assigning each point to its nearest centroid, and (2) re-computing centroids as the arithmetic mean of assigned points. The algorithm is guaranteed to converge to a local minimum.

models/kmeans_plus_plus/index.html.step1_desc: K-Means++ replaces random centroid initialization with a probabilistic scheme where probability of choosing point $x$ as the next centroid is proportional to its squared distance to the nearest existing centroid.
models/kmeans_plus_plus/index.html.step2_desc: Ensures initial centroids are well spread out across the feature space, eliminating poor initializations and guaranteeing an $O(\log K)$ approximation ratio to optimal clustering.

models/kmedoids_clustering/index.html.step1_formula: $$\mathcal{J}_{\text{Medoids}} = \sum_{k=1}^K \sum_{x \in C_k} d(x, m_k), \quad m_k \in X \text{ (exact exemplar data point)}$$
models/kmedoids_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Requires cluster centers to be actual data points (medoids) rather than arbitrary arithmetic averages, drastically increasing robustness against extreme outliers and arbitrary distance metrics.
models/kmedoids_clustering/index.html.step2_formula: $$\Delta T_{ih} = \sum_{j} \left( d(x_j, m_{\text{new}}) - d(x_j, m_{\text{old}}) \right) < 0 \implies m_k \leftarrow x_h$$
models/kmedoids_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: Iteratively evaluates swapping a medoid $m_i$ with non-medoid point $x_h$. The swap is executed if total configuration cost $\Delta T < 0$, converging when no improving swap exists.

models/fuzzy_c_means/index.html.step1_title: Soft Membership Degree Objective with Fuzzifier m
models/fuzzy_c_means/index.html.step1_desc: Assigns data points soft degrees of membership $u_{ik}$ to all clusters, enabling realistic modeling of overlapping boundaries. Parameter $m$ controls cluster fuzziness.
models/fuzzy_c_means/index.html.step2_title: Alternating Optimality Conditions for Membership & Centers
models/fuzzy_c_means/index.html.step2_formula: $$u_{ik} = \frac{1}{\sum_{j=1}^C \left(\frac{\|x_i - c_k\|}{\|x_i - c_j\|}\right)^{\frac{2}{m-1}}}, \quad c_k = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n u_{ik}^m x_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n u_{ik}^m}$$
models/fuzzy_c_means/index.html.step2_desc: Derived via Lagrange multipliers: membership $u_{ik}$ decreases smoothly with distance to center $c_k$, while centers $c_k$ are weighted barycenters.

models/agglomerative_hierarchical/index..step1_title: Pairwise Cluster Distance & Ward's Minimum Variance
models/agglomerative_hierarchical/index..step1_desc: Begins with $n$ singleton clusters and iteratively merges the pair $(A, B)$ that minimizes the increase in total within-cluster variance (Ward's criterion).
models/agglomerative_hierarchical/index..step2_formula: $$D(A \cup B, C) = \alpha_A D(A, C) + \alpha_B D(B, C) + \beta D(A, B) + \gamma |D(A, C) - D(B, C)|$$
models/agglomerative_hierarchical/index..step2_desc: Allows updating distance matrices in $O(1)$ time per merge for Single, Complete, Average, and Ward linkages without recomputing raw point distances.

models/divisive_hierarchical/index.html.step1_desc: Starts with all $n$ data points in a single giant root cluster and iteratively splits the cluster with the largest diameter into subclusters (DIANA algorithm).
models/divisive_hierarchical/index.html.step2_formula: $$\Delta D(x) = \frac{1}{|A| - 1} \sum_{y \in A \setminus \{x\}} d(x, y) - \frac{1}{|B|} \sum_{z \in B} d(x, z) > 0 \implies x \to B$$
models/divisive_hierarchical/index.html.step2_desc: Creates a splinter group $B$ by selecting the point with highest average dissimilarity to its peers, iteratively pulling remaining points closer to $B$ than to $A$.

models/dbscan_clustering/index.html.step1_formula: $$\mathcal{N}_\epsilon(p) = \{q \in D \mid d(p, q) \le \epsilon\}, \quad p \text{ is Core} \iff |\mathcal{N}_\epsilon(p)| \ge \text{MinPts}$$
models/dbscan_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Defines density as the number of data points residing within radius $\epsilon$. Points meeting threshold $\text{MinPts}$ are designated as dense Core points.
models/dbscan_clustering/index.html.step2_formula: $$p \leftrightarrow q \iff \exists o_1, \dots, o_k \text{ s.t. } o_1 = p, o_k = q, \; o_{i+1} \in \mathcal{N}_\epsilon(o_i) \text{ and Core}(o_i)$$
models/dbscan_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: Clusters are maximal sets of density-connected points. Points that are neither core nor within $\epsilon$ of a core point are formally isolated as Noise ($label = -1$).

models/hdbscan_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Transforms metric space such that low-density points are pushed far apart from each other, robustly preventing chaining effects across sparse regions.
models/hdbscan_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: Constructs a Minimum Spanning Tree over mutual reachability distances, condensing it into a hierarchy and extracting the flat clusters with maximum excess stability.

models/optics_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Extends DBSCAN to accommodate variable density clusters by ordering points such that spatially closest dense neighbors appear adjacently in an ordered list.
models/optics_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: Plots reachability distance in execution order. Dips and valleys in the reachability graph directly represent dense clusters separated by high reachability peaks.

models/mean_shift_clustering/index.html.step1_formula: $$\hat{f}(x) = \frac{1}{n b^p} \sum_{i=1}^n K\left( \frac{x - x_i}{b} \right), \quad K(u) = c_{k, d} \cdot k(\|u\|^2)$$
models/mean_shift_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Treats the feature space as an empirical probability density function using a radially symmetric kernel $K$ with bandwidth $b$.
models/mean_shift_clustering/index.html.step2_title: Mean Shift Vector Density Gradient Ascent
models/mean_shift_clustering/index.html.step2_formula: $$m(x) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n K\left(\frac{x - x_i}{b}\right) x_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n K\left(\frac{x - x_i}{b}\right)} - x \propto \frac{\nabla \hat{f}(x)}{\hat{f}(x)} \implies x^{(t+1)} = x^{(t)} + m(x^{(t)})$$
models/mean_shift_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: The mean shift vector $m(x)$ points in the direction of maximum increase in local point density. Points climb the gradient until converging onto stationary peak modes.

models/gaussian_mixture_models/index.htm.step1_desc: Models continuous data as a convex mixture of $K$ multivariate Gaussian components, each with its own prior weight $\pi_k$, mean vector $\mu_k$, and full covariance matrix $\Sigma_k$.
models/gaussian_mixture_models/index.htm.step2_desc: Alternates between: (E-step) estimating posterior responsibilities $\gamma_{ik}$ that component $k$ generated point $x_i$, and (M-step) updating means, covariances, and mixing weights.

models/spectral_clustering/index.html.step1_formula: $$W_{ij} = \exp\left( -\frac{\|x_i - x_j\|^2}{2\sigma^2} \right), \quad D_{ii} = \sum_{j} W_{ij}, \quad L_{\text{sym}} = I - D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2}$$
models/spectral_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Builds a continuous similarity graph $W$ with degree diagonal matrix $D$, constructing the normalized symmetric graph Laplacian $L_{\text{sym}}$ representing graph cut energetics.
models/spectral_clustering/index.html.step2_formula: $$L_{\text{sym}} v_i = \lambda_i v_i \implies U = [v_1, v_2, \dots, v_K] \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times K}, \quad \hat{y} = \text{K-Means}(U_{\text{norm}})$$
models/spectral_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: The $K$ eigenvectors corresponding to the smallest eigenvalues project non-convex manifold structures into linearly separable coordinates where standard K-Means succeeds.

models/affinity_propagation/index.html.step1_formula: $$s(i, k) = -\|x_i - x_k\|^2 \quad (i \ne k), \quad s(k, k) = \text{median}(\{s(i, j)\}) = p$$
models/affinity_propagation/index.html.step1_desc: Measures pairwise affinity $s(i, k)$ between all point pairs. Diagonal entries $s(k, k)$ act as preferences; higher values increase the likelihood of point $k$ becoming an exemplar.
models/affinity_propagation/index.html.step2_formula: $$r(i, k) \leftarrow s(i, k) - \max_{k' \ne k} \{a(i, k') + s(i, k')\}, \quad a(i, k) \leftarrow \min\left(0, \, r(k, k) + \sum_{i' \notin \{i, k\}} \max(0, r(i', k))\right)$$
models/affinity_propagation/index.html.step2_desc: Points iteratively exchange real-valued messages until convergence: responsibility $r(i, k)$ evaluates exemplar suitability, and availability $a(i, k)$ reflects peer endorsement.

models/birch_clustering/index.html.step1_desc: Compresses arbitrary subclusters into compact zero-th, first, and second order statistical moments $(N, \vec{LS}, SS)$, satisfying linear additivity $\text{CF}_1 + \text{CF}_2 = (N_1+N_2, \vec{LS}_1+\vec{LS}_2, SS_1+SS_2)$.
models/birch_clustering/index.html.step2_desc: Streams data points through an in-memory height-balanced CF-tree in a single $O(n)$ scan, inserting points into existing leaf entries if cluster radius $R \le T$, followed by global clustering.
